# `←` — Assign

Syntax. Keys: `Alt-h`. Hanzi: `是`

`N←Y` binds the name `N` to `Y`, an array, function or operator, and returns `Y` without displaying it. The target is the run just before `←`, and the value is everything to its right. Independent assignments need `⋄`, as in `a←1 ⋄ b←2`.

```bpl
x←3 ⋄ x+2          ⍝ 5
x←1+2 × 3 ⋄ x      ⍝ 9
sum←+/ ⋄ sum 1 2 3 ⍝ 6
```

`N f←Y` sets `N` to `N f Y`. A named function goes in parentheses, `N(f)←Y`, because in `N f←Y` the target would be `f`. With nothing after the arrow, `N f←` sets `N` to `f N`.

```bpl
x←10 ⋄ x+←3 ⋄ x    ⍝ 13
f←× ⋄ x←3 ⋄ x(f)←4 ⋄ x ⍝ 12
x←1 2 3 ⋄ x⌽← ⋄ x ⍝ 3 2 1
```

A target can also be a [subscript](../scripts.ipynb#subscripts) such as `x₁`, a [dot](dot.qmd) path such as `T.a` or `x.[i]`, or a selection, `(f N)`, where `f` only selects or rearranges, as for structural [Under](at.qmd). A space before `←` makes the whole run before it the target, as parentheses would, so `2↑x ←8 9` is `(2↑x)←8 9`. Modified assignment applies its function to each selected item. To apply a function to a selection as a whole, use Under, as in `m(⌽@ 1⌷)←` or `m←⌽@ 1⌷ m`. `[a b]←Y` destructures by position: each name gets the matching item. A pattern takes items by key: in `[top: k:b]←Y`, `top` gets the item with key `"top"` and `b` the item with key `"k"`.

```bpl
x←1 2 3 ⋄ x₁←9 ⋄ x ⍝ 1 9 3
x←1 2 3 ⋄ x.[[0 2]]+←10 ⋄ x ⍝ 11 2 13
x←1 2 3 ⋄ (2↑x)←8 9 ⋄ x ⍝ 8 9 3
x←1 2 3 ⋄ 2↑x ←8 9 ⋄ x ⍝ 8 9 3
[a b]←10 20 ⋄ a+b  ⍝ 30
[top: k:b]←["top":1 "k":2] ⋄ top b ⍝ 1 2
```

Inside a dfn, plain assignment is local. Modified and selective assignment update the nearest existing binding. [Assignment](../assignment.ipynb) covers every form.
